source: us-counties: {"boundaries":"US Census Bureau cb_2022_us_county_20m","svi":"CDC/ATSDR SVI 2022 county (ACS 2018-2022)","places":"CDC PLACES county data, 2024 release (model-based estimates from BRFSS 2022; a few measures BRFSS 2021)","ers":"USDA ERS Rural-Urban Continuum Codes 2023; Unemployment & median household income file (BLS LAUS, Census SAIPE)"}; us-county-mortality: NHTSA FARS 2017-2023 final annual files (static.nhtsa.gov/nhtsa/downloads/FARS), public domain; population: US Census 2020 via USDA ERS
licence: Public domain: US Census Bureau cb_2022 boundaries, CDC/ATSDR SVI 2022, USDA ERS / BLS LAUS unemployment; traffic deaths: NHTSA FARS 2017-2023, public domain
note: All counties in IL (17), IN (18), OH (39), MI (26), WI (55), in source FIPS order. Queen uses all source parts, shared vertices rounded to 4 decimals; islands: 0. knn6 is directed, using full-precision source centroids and haversine distance, ties by subset index; CSR neighbors sorted by index. Centroids rounded to 4 decimals. Unemployment values are percentages, rounded to 2 decimals. deaths counts motor-vehicle crash deaths in the county of crash (FARS), 2017-2023 total, not all-cause mortality; deaths2023 is the 2023 count; personYears is seven times 2020 Census residents, while population is ACS 2018-2022. Largest part only, ranked by absolute exterior shoelace area minus holes, scaled by cos(mean latitude); holes of that part retained. Duplicate closing vertices removed; "ringsClosed": false. No simplification beyond coordinate rounding. Display geometry is in s2-midwest-county-shapes.json, rounded to 3 decimals; queen remains computed at 4 decimals.
